subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: What session-health breaker contract should OpenClaw core own before implementation: a unified receipt/state model, a narrow no-progress counter, or deferral to existing narrower guard tracks?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested behavior crosses failure taxonomy, config defaults, persisted session state, recovery actions, UI/operator surfacing, and existing retry policy, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Design unified session-health receipts
options.body: Define failure signature, counters, last success, retry admission, suggested recovery, persistence, and operator recovery semantics before implementation.

options.title: Land a narrow no-progress breaker
options.body: Limit the first change to a bounded consecutive no-progress counter in the embedded run loop and leave receipts, persistence, cooldowns, and auto-rotation for follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to narrower guards
options.body: Keep idle-timeout, compaction, tool-loop, provider, cron, and subagent breaker tracks separate and close or narrow this umbrella request later.

recommendation.title: Design unified session-health receipts
recommendation.body: Define failure signature, counters, last success, retry admission, suggested recovery, persistence, and operator recovery semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows repeated adjacent retry, liveness, and breaker-path work, making this the best available owner for the product contract choice.
